newsitem.title: USA: Amoco, PS Enterprise to share Colombia power plant.
newsitem.headline: Amoco, PS Enterprise to share Colombia power plant.

text.p: Subsidiaries of Amoco Corp and Public Service Enterprise Group Inc said they agreed to jointly own a 200 megawatt (MW) electricity generating station in Colombia.

The Termo Santander de Colombia plant, which is being developed by Amoco Power, will be owned 50 percent by each company, Amoco's Amoco Power Resources Corp and Public Service's Community Energy Alternatives Inc said.

The sale of Amoco's initial 100 percent interest in the plant is in compliance with Colombian law which prohibits natural gas producers from owning more than 50 percent of a gas-fired power plant after the date of commercial operations, the companies said in a statement.
Termo Santander will be built at the Opon natgas field operated by Amoco, about 125 miles north of Bogota, Colombia.
Plant construction began in January and it is expected to begin commercial operations by the end of 1997.
The plant, which will produce enough electricity to power a city of 70,000 people, will sell its electrical output into the Colombian spot electricity market, the companies said.
Termo Santander will consume up to 60 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from the Opon field.
